newsitem.title: ITALY: Major says unlikely all countries ready for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Major says unlikely all countries ready for EMU.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said in an interview published on Friday that it was unlikely but not impossible that all countries would be able to meet criteria on time for the second phase of monetary union.
"The fact is that there are still many uncertainties in the project of monetary union," he said in an interview with Milan's Corriere della Sera.
The interview was published to coincide with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi's visit to London on Friday.

"The most serious (uncertainty) is that it appears always more unlikely, although not impossible, that the ability of countries to meet Maastricht criteria will be sufficiently clear and stable for the punctual start of phase two of monetary union," he was quoted as saying in the Italian translation of the interview.
The euro is due to be launched at the start of the second phase in 1999.
"We will not want to take part in a single currency which is launched without a safe level of sustainable convergence," he was quoted as saying.
He repeated that it would be very important to outline future relations between countries taking part in monetary union and those not taking part.
"All these points must be clear to us before making a decision of such importance such as, taking part in monetary union," he was was quoted as saying.

Major's conservatives have insisted on a wait-and-see policy on Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), although the government admitted earlier this month that it was very unlikely Britain would participate in the first wave of countries in two years' time.
